gap: No result ChatGPT got states what either unit costs today: on BLUETTI's US store the Apex 200 is $1,099 and the Apex 300 is $1,499, so the Apex 300 costs $400 more alone and with one B300K ($2,199 vs $2,599). Connecting the Apex 300 to the house panel adds a $699 Apex 300-only Home Integration Kit, and BLUETTI lists no panel kit for the Apex 200.
standout_why: I compared against the cited BLUETTI comparison blog (bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/apex-200-vs-apex-300, read 2026-11-17). It gives no dollar figure for any model, battery or transfer hardware. It says only that 'The Apex 300 is priced higher than the Apex 200' and mentions transfer equipment without naming a model. ChatGPT's cited product pages carry the price, but ChatGPT still said it 'couldn't verify a comparable live base-unit price' for the Apex 200. The only price it showed was FactoryPure's $1,374.99 Apex 300, and FactoryPure's store lists that item as unavailable today. No cited page prices the panel kit or says the kit fits the Apex 300 only.
decides: ChatGPT made its pick depend on whether the Apex 200 'offers meaningful savings'. The answer is $400 on the base unit and $400 with one B300K. It is $550 at the B500K bundle level, and buying the Apex 200 and B500K separately ($2,698) is $51 cheaper than BLUETTI's own Apex 200 + B500K bundle. For a backup wired into the house panel, the Apex 300 is the only one with a BLUETTI kit: $1,499 + $699 = $2,198. The Apex 200's maker page describes no panel connection and names only a TT-30R and a 12 V/30 A Anderson port. This supports ChatGPT's pick of the Apex 300 for a panel-connected or 240 V home backup, and leaves the Apex 200 as the $400-cheaper choice for 120 V plug-in essentials. Both units now ship in late January, so neither is in stock. Our page's 'Ships from Nov 20' and 'In stock' cells are out of date.
